newsitem.title: USA: Illinois rains improve corn, soybean crop outlook.
newsitem.headline: Illinois rains improve corn, soybean crop outlook.

text.p: Rains in Illinois during the week to Sunday improved the outlook for corn and soybean crops although warmer weather is needed, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.
"The latest rainfall has most reporters optimistic about the crop but the general consensus is that warm weather is needed for crops to make good progress," the report said.
Corn had an average height of six inches, up from the five-year average of four inches. It was rated 10 percent excellent, 58 pct good, 30 pct fair and two pct poor.
Soybeans were 92 percent planted, up slightly from 89 percent a week earlier, with fieldwork slowed by the showers.
The total was still up sharply from the five-year average of 56 percent, and the last time it was this advanced as of June 1 was in 1988.

Winter wheat was 87 percent headed and 38 percent filled, marginally behind the five-year averages of 89 and 41 percent respectively. It was rated six percent excellent, 66 percent good, 24 percent fair, three percent poor and one percent very poor.
